activity_context.topic_title: Symmetry Properties of the Standard Normal Distribution

feedback.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(-0.19<Z<0.38).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/bd478e9925303e3d018e2d070e4e3a78e72fb699a48ac3109ddf743158bb5599.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.19<Z<0.38) & =P(Z<0.38)-P(Z\le -0.19) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.38)-P(Z\le -0.19) \\  & =Φ(0.38)-Φ(-0.19)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.38) & =0.3520 \\ Φ(-0.19) & =0.4247,\end{aligned}
$$

but we are not given $Φ(0.38).$ However, we can compute this using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.38) & =P(Z\le 0.38) \\  & =P(Z\ge -0.38) \\  & =1-P(Z<-0.38) \\  & =1-P(Z\le -0.38) \\  & =1-Φ(-0.38) \\  & =1-0.3520 \\  & =0.6480\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.19<Z<0.38) & =Φ(0.38)-Φ(-0.19) \\  & =0.6480-0.4247 \\  & =0.2233.\end{aligned}
$$
